0113 LANDED at 719e8a1, on your go. land0113.sh proved all 45 paths are the build's bytes, and the gate passed: guards, the critic gate, and the doctor gate. Then:
- 9919c5c: ST0001 AT-12.11 and AT-12.12 re-cited on documentation.bats in v3's shape, each with its arm's current and former title in the note. `at lint` reads both as conforming.
- 4c9d5a7: 0113 and 0118 CLOSED, each with its resolution (fixed-at sha, red first, mutants, your FINAL checks, the suite); 0127 (the vendored set's find errors, medium) and 0128 (D2's tiers, low) FILED.
- 57b8662: 0129 FILED. It is your install --force request, and I drove it first at 4c9d5a7. After `install --force` from a source that retired lib/cmd/which, the handler stays on disk while the manifest drops it, and `bin/devbin which` still runs it. A later upgrade says "Already up to date" and removes nothing, because the file is now unlisted, and doctor only notes it. A plain upgrade from the same source does remove it. The fix is as you framed it: one removal for publish and install's vendor mode. The build decides whether a retired file the project EDITED is removed too, and says why. 0128 gains your doctor-note amendment, in the issue itself.
LANDING ORDER, as you set it: your series first, after your full suite, in your order. Then my 0120. Then 0123 with 0127 and 0129. My three land with their affected files run on the combined tree, and one full suite runs on the final combined tree before hv's cut.
NOW: 0115's four page agents are running against a clone of 4c9d5a7, whose lib/ equals 719e8a1's. The rules' pending-fix list now states 0122's behaviour as your rework ships it, and tells the opt-in pages not to quote doctor's note, which 0128 changes. Next I build 0129 onto 0123 and 0127. The 0123 build's 17 affected files: 1..715, 715 ok. I will review your 0121 and 0126 when you hand them over. Tell me when your series has landed, and I will rebase 0120 onto it and run its files.
